title: introduce-mini-fastlane-presubmit-and-dependency-metrics-adapter
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Our full presubmit lanes are costly and provide slow feedback for small, targeted changes. This PR introduces a lightweight 'mini-fastlane' presubmit lane that runs a compact set of checks selected by a change-sensitive heuristics scorer, and a new dependency-metrics-adapter service that exports simple dependency health signals to our telemetry pipeline. Motivation: speed up developer feedback for small edits, reduce CI cost, and provide early visibility into dependency rot/vuln hotspots across affected packages. What this PR does: 1) mini-fastlane presubmit runner: - New GH Actions workflow .github/workflows/mini-fastlane.yml that runs fast checks for PRs with low impact diff by using a change classifier (rust/python/ts path heuristics + diff size thresholds). - Implements file-pattern scoring so affected-language specific linters (eslint, go vet, pyflakes) and a small test subset run instead of full matrix. - Adds a presubmit opt-out annotation (ci:full) for cases that still need full validation. 2) dependency-metrics-adapter: - A small Go binary (cmd/dep-metrics-adapter) that parses lockfiles (package-lock.json, go.sum, poetry.lock) and computes simple signals: lockfile_age_days, transitive_depth_estimate, unresolved_version_count, and a computed staleness_score. - Exposes /metrics (Prometheus) and periodic export to our telemetry pipeline (http POST to telemetry ingestion). - Lightweight policy: warns on staleness_score >= 0.7 for packages touched by the PR. 3) Refactor: - Extracts the language routing logic from the monolithic presubmit runner into a plugin interface (pkg/presubmit/plugin) so future lanes can be composed with the mini-fastlane logic. - Moves several bash init scripts to small Go CLIs to reduce flakiness in runners. Rollout plan: - Step 1 (canary): Enable mini-fastlane for label-friendly repos and 30% of PRs in redwood/* for 48 hours behind a feature flag. - Step 2: Observe CI cost delta and time-to-green; if <10% regression in test coverage signal, expand to 75% for 7 days. - Step 3: Default to opt-in across repo groups; allow toggling via repo settings and annotation. Operator notes: - mini-fastlane will skip heavyweight integration tests by default; these remain gated under the full presubmit. - To force full validation add the PR body line: ci:full. Testing performed: - Local integration with dockerized runners and a simulated 50k-line repo to validate classification heuristics. - E2E smoke on redwood/examples with 60 sample PRs; median feedback reduced from 12m -> 3.8m for mini-fastlane eligible PRs. - Unit tests for dep-metrics-adapter included; mocked telemetry ingestion used in CI. Security & privacy: - dep-metrics-adapter uses only repo-local lockfiles and does not send source diffs outside telemetry; telemetry payloads are aggregated counts and package names only. Checklist: - [x] add GH workflow and documentation (docs/ci/mini-fastlane.md) - [x] implement presubmit plugin interface - [x] add dep-metrics-adapter and Prometheus metrics - [x] add integration + unit tests - [x] add rollout feature flag in infra/flags.md Backlinks: Linear ENG-2781 (mini-fastlane), ENG-2782 (dep-metrics telemetry). Commands to exercise locally: - make dev-presubmit-run TARGET=mini - ./bin/dep-metrics-adapter --scan . --dry-run Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the whitelist of checks conservative (lint + fast unit tests + typecheck) to avoid false negatives. Future work: integrate vulnerability scanner scores and surface suggested bump PRs, add language-specific learned classifiers for file importance.

release_notes: Introduce mini-fastlane presubmit for faster feedback on small diffs; add dependency-metrics-adapter to export simple dep-health signals to telemetry; refactor presubmit runner into plugin interface for composability.
